title: Per-application configuration
description: Everything app-specific the tool needs, in one file per application (security/dast/<app_id>/app.yaml). Onboarding an application is adding one of these — never a code change (see docs/dast_poc_remediation_plan.md §1). This is an INPUT: generate still emits the frozen artifacts (scope.json, auth.json, zap-policy.yaml, manifest.json, lock) from it, so preflight and the runner are unchanged. Credentials appear only as environment variable NAMES (NFR-3). additionalProperties is false everywhere so a typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.

app_id.description: Application id; must match the directory name and the app_id on every detection record.

environment_class.description: Deliberately has no default: preflight refuses prod (D3), and a wrong value here is the whole safety story, so it must be stated per app rather than inherited.

base_url.description: The target as ZAP resolves it (D7), e.g. http://juice:3000 on the compose network.

allow.description: Hosts that may be reached AND attacked. Exact match, case-insensitive (D6). A bare host (`app.internal`) admits that host on every scheme and port; an origin (`https://app.internal:8443`) admits exactly that scheme, host and port, default ports normalised (W4-2). test and staging environments must use origins — preflight refuses bare hosts there, since every port of a shared machine is not 'in scope'.

deny.description: Wildcard deny patterns; deny takes precedence over allow (D6).

avoid_actions.description: Destructive action terms refused deterministically during exploration (never by LLM judgement).

exclude.description: Endpoints the scanner must never touch, by path (W4-5) — mail, SMS, payments, partner systems, resets. Each covers the path and everything beneath it (`/api/payments` covers `/api/payments/42`, not `/api/paymentsx`); `*` matches within one segment; case-insensitive. Enforced on ZAP's spider and active scan, in the per-scan ZAP context, and during exploration. Each one is a detection gap to disclose.

auth.description: How to log in and how we PROVE we are logged in. Operator-owned: the LLM never sees or influences this block. Give either `selectors` (the three-field shorthand) or `steps` (anything else: a username field, a two-page login, a keypress) — the shorthand normalizes into steps.

mode.description: form = drive the login form; seeded = replay a human-seeded storageState.

selectors.description: Shorthand for the common single-step form: fill identifier, fill secret, click submit. Equivalent to the three-step `steps` list.

proof.description: Exactly one proof of authentication, and no default — an unproven session must never be scanned. js: a truthy JS expression (SPA with a visible token). route: an authenticated route must answer 2xx/3xx and not bounce to the login page (cookie sessions, where no token is reachable from JavaScript). selector: an element that only exists when logged in.

js.description: JS expression that is truthy only when authenticated, e.g. window.localStorage.getItem('token').

path.description: An authenticated route to probe, e.g. /account.

expect_status.description: Exact status to require; any 2xx/3xx if omitted.

forbid_redirect_to.description: Substring that must NOT appear in the landing URL, e.g. login.php.

selector.description: CSS selector present only when authenticated, e.g. nav a[href='/logout'].

identity.description: provisioned (default): a test account already exists. self-register: the tool may create its own account via auth.bootstrap — most real applications forbid this.

bootstrap.description: Account-creation request, used only when identity is self-register. Credentials are injected from the environment at run time.

body.description: Extra body fields merged with the credential fields.

credentials.description: Environment variable NAMES only — never values (NFR-3).

storage_state.description: Where the seeded session lives (W5-3): a file path (git-ignored, mode 600, re-seeded after storage_state_ttl_hours), or `env:VAR` — the storageState JSON, raw or base64, delivered by a secret store and written to disk only for the run.

steps.description: The login as an ordered list of browser actions — the general form. Values are never written here: `value` names which credential to type, and the credential itself comes from the environment (NFR-3).

value.description: Which credential to type (fill only). email/password are accepted as aliases of identifier/secret.

key.description: Key to press (press only), e.g. Enter.

cookies.description: Cookies to seed into the scanning browser before replay, e.g. {security: low}. Some applications keep test-relevant state in a cookie the scanner would otherwise never set — DVWA's security level is one, and not setting it silently changed a five-finding scan into a zero-finding one. State the scan depends on belongs in configuration, not in luck. Never put a credential or a session token here (W6-8).

storage_state_ttl_hours.description: How old a stored session FILE may be before it is refused and must be re-seeded (W5-3). Default 12.

bearer_from_cookie.description: A cookie whose value the application also expects as `Authorization: Bearer …`. After a mid-scan re-login (W5-2) both are rewritten on ZAP's attacks. Juice Shop: `token`.

dismiss_selectors.description: Cookie banners / welcome modals to click away before interacting. Empty for a new application — nothing is inherited from another app's UI.

authenticated_routes.description: Routes the recorded walk visits after login, chosen so the SPA fires its authenticated XHR.

patterns.description: URL substrings that mark a request as an API call worth recording, e.g. /rest/ or /v1/.

safe_forms.description: Targets for which a state-changing submit is permitted (SP-1). Empty = read-only exploration.

submit_get_forms.description: Whether exploration may submit forms that explicitly use GET. Submitting a search or filter form is how an endpoint's parameters become visible to the scanner, and a GET submit is a read. Set false for an application known to mutate on GET; state-changing verbs are default-denied either way.

write_mode.description: Whether exploration may submit state-changing forms (POST/PUT/PATCH). Permitted only when data_policy is disposable. Unlocks stored XSS, POST-body injection, mass assignment and upload flaws, which are invisible to a read-only scan (SP-1). DELETE always needs an explicit safe_forms entry, and session-ending actions are refused at any posture.

test_data.description: Field name -> value to type when filling a form, e.g. {email: dast@example.test, search: test}. Posting empty strings mostly yields validation errors rather than coverage, so approved test data is what makes write mode worth enabling.

scan.description: Scan posture for this application. These are deliberate choices, not defaults to inherit: attack strength and alert threshold govern depth and noise, and every exclusion here is a detection gap that must be disclosed when results are compared with another tool (readiness SP-1..SP-5).

disabled_rules.description: ZAP plugin ids to switch off, each one a disclosed gap.

state_probes.description: Paths fetched before the scan whose responses are hashed into the coverage artifact, so two scans can be compared for whether the application was in the same condition. Only a digest is stored (W6-8).

throttle.description: How hard the scan may push the application (W4-3). A shared environment has other users; ZAP's defaults are tuned for throughput. Unset keeps ZAP's defaults.

threads_per_host.description: Concurrent active-scan threads per host; also the spider's thread count.

delay_ms.description: Delay between active-scan requests, in milliseconds.

liveness_path.description: A path whose answer differs when logged in, probed through ZAP at most once a minute during the active scan (W5-1). A redirect to the login page, a 401/403, or the logged-out answer means the session was lost, and the health gate fails. Default: auth.proof.route.path, else the first scan.state_probes entry; with neither, liveness is recorded as unknown.

reauth.description: Re-establish a session lost mid-scan by logging in again (W5-2): the active scan is paused, the login replayed the way the scan first authenticated, ZAP's attacks pointed at the new session, and the scan resumed. The loss is still recorded and the scan marked degraded, so no finding can resolve from it. Without it — or past `max` — a loss stops the scan.

anti_csrf_tokens.description: Anti-CSRF form field names ZAP should refresh for each attack, beyond its built-in list (W5-2). Without this, attacks replay a used token, the app rejects them, and some apps log the session out.

data_policy.description: Whether this environment's data can be thrown away and rebuilt. `durable` (the default) means writes are refused: a scan must not corrupt data other people depend on. `disposable` is an attestation by whoever owns the environment, and it is what write mode requires — the decision belongs to a person, once per application, not to a model per form.

output.description: Where this application's artifacts are written. Overridden per machine by --out or $DAST_OUT, because this file is committed and shared.

dir.description: Directory holding <app>/authoring, <app>/scans and <app>/state.json. Relative paths resolve from the repository root, never the current directory. ~ and ${VAR} expand, so a committed config can stay portable. Default: out

publish.description: Where findings are published. Publishing still requires an explicit --upload: it is a one-way door and config alone never triggers it.

ref.description: Ref of the DEPLOYED build that was scanned, e.g. refs/heads/main. No default: GitHub shows it on every alert as the affected branch. Usually supplied per run by --ref or $DAST_TARGET_REF rather than committed here.

category.description: Automation category separating this application's analysis from another's. GitHub keys an analysis by (tool, category, ref), so two applications sharing one must not share a category or the newer upload replaces the older one's alerts. Default: dast/<app_id>

commit.description: Full SHA of the DEPLOYED build that was scanned. No default — the scanner's own checkout is not the target (W1-8). Usually supplied per run by --commit or $DAST_TARGET_COMMIT from the deploy pipeline, since it changes every deploy; set it here only for a pinned target.

evidence_url.description: Where each alert links for its stored request/response (W1-4). Either a per-file template using {scan_id} and {path} (an organisation's own artifact store), or a page that holds the evidence, such as a CI run — a GitHub artifact is a zip, so that link reaches the run and the alert names the file inside it. Overridden by --evidence-url or $DAST_EVIDENCE_URL. Unset: alerts name the file instead of linking.

gate.description: When `dast report` fails the build. Findings that already existed are somebody's decision; only NEW ones can fail it.

fail_on.description: Fail (exit 1) when a NEW finding is at or above this severity. Overridden by --fail-on or $DAST_FAIL_ON. Default: high. `none` disables the gate.
